newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso plunges to record closing low.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso plunges to record closing low.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed above eight to the dollar for the first time ever on Wednesday after another speculative onslaught and exodus of foreign investors, traders said.
"Lack of confidence among foreign investors is dragging us down towards a situation as bleak as last year," said a trader, recalling peso volatility throughout 1995.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both closed 6.5 centavos weaker at 7.9800/8.000 and 7.9850/8.0050 per dollar, respectively.
The same-day peso had closed earlier 8.7 centavos weaker at 7.9800/8.00 per dollar.
"It's the same old story, we know it by heart," said another trader.

Traders noted that foreign investors had stepped out of the Mexican money and stock markets in droves. This happened despite the fact that domestic interest rates had risen sharply at Tuesday night's primary auction and the sharp recent fall in U.S. long bond yields.
Bellwether 28-day Cetes rates gained 164 basis points to 29.34 percent at the Banco de Mexico auction Tuesday.
The 30-year Treasury bond yield was meanwhile at 6.69 percent.
Stocks were also hit by foreign investors bailing out. The blue chip IPC index was down 42.31 points, or 1.32 percent, at 3,156.77 when the foreign exchange market closed.
"Jacking up rates to bolster the peso is not working any more," said a trader. "When rates soar, it's a sign that things are wrong in a country."
"Without meaning to, (rate hikes) can have the opposite effect, as foreign investment is shunned by a higher risk perception," said another trader.
Dealers felt the peso could trade at above 8.10 per dollar in the coming weeks, due to uncertainty over forthcoming U.S. presidential elections and the Fed Open Market Committee meeting.
